sourceScope: Runtime/build/test/Demo/Usage/consumer declared inputs agree across Windows/live and Linux/frozen copies. Later general-doc edits are outside these validated inputs.
nativeBridgeScope: Qualified subset: nine original native point readings, scalar provider actions, physical screen bounds and next/previous paging on Windows UIA and private-session Linux AT-SPI. Full native qualification and Windows root selected-item array remain false. Synthetic provider calls are not physical device or reader speech validation.
remaining: Physical keyboard and actual NVDA/Narrator/Orca speech/automatic announcement have not been qualified; external native tree/provider tests do not imply a complete screen-reader workflow.
Native Windows FocusedElement remains the CartesianChart while the virtual CurrentPoint reports focus and the chart Value summary includes its reading; per-point native system focus remains open.

HighContrastMode and ReduceMotion are application-supplied. Host applications must bridge operating-system/user preferences explicitly; local styles and explicit series brushes preserve precedence and may lower contrast.

Default accessible source page64, requested maximum256 and chart-owned LRU256 bound internal materialization. External clients holding evicted peers can retain old source items/series/chart; total native/client-held memory is not capped by that LRU.

Keyboard search is bounded to4096 source values per directional candidate search. A far-reordered identity without an existing identity index is explicitly unavailable rather than building a million-item index on demand.

Summary count first evaluation for each new snapshot still scans the mapped canonical data on the UI thread. UIA/AT-SPI traversal/event floods, million-point interactive latency, native client retention and memory/soak budgets remain C4 qualification.

Category legends/legend virtualization, overview navigator/cross-chart cursors, label leader-lines/advanced collision handling and independent per-series animation delay/progress remain follow-up work.
Animation stationary-pointer readings do not continuously follow moving data. Future chart-family geometry, exit fades and stagger transitions remain open.
Independent nullable-auto axes within four-bound Viewport remain limited; the known multi-axis title/end-tick collision at the Demo top-right remains open.
Physical Windows/Linux devices, Ubuntu22.04/24.04, native Wayland/ARM, multi-screen/high-DPI interaction, actual GPU/backend/compositor presentation and licensed official runtime remain open.

Export capture/copy executes on the UI thread and compression cannot be preempted within the codec call. Save-picker real interaction, encoding throughput/peak memory/concurrent-chart/soak budgets remain open.

JPEG is lossy; exact original-color thin-stroke equality is not guaranteed and no independent chroma-subsampling option exists. Lossless PNG exact and registered lossy geometry relations are separate gates.
Inherited four missing original v15 BarCache.PixelProbe.dll artifacts remain open; no rebuilt substitutes were used.

Windows root SelectionPattern.GetSelection returns an empty native array despite one selected item. The same result occurs with an attached real ControlPeer selector; exact bridge/SDK root cause and a public-API fix remain open.
Windows actual FocusedElement remains CartesianChart; virtual point focus and readable chart current-value summary do not certify system per-point focus or automatic reader announcements.

Linux fixture seed verifies native selected count and point Selected state, but get_selected_child(0) returns null and selected-child enumeration remains open; select_child(0) addresses a direct series checkbox, not a nested point. Native nested point selection write and actual Orca navigation/speech remain open.
Actual NVDA/Narrator/Orca speech, physical devices, multi-screen DPI and native Wayland/Linux distributions beyond this WSLg session remain open.
